messages:
Ava (CS): heads up — Everset reported prompt crossover between concurrent sessions in prod last night. Portions of one user's prompt leaking into another user's response. They say it's reproducible with parallel requests.

Ava (CS): repro steps from the customer:
```
# session A
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \n  -H "x-session-id: evs-user-42" \n  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Order pizza with pepperoni"}]}'
# session B sent at same time
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \n  -H "x-session-id: evs-user-42-b" \n  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Book a flight to SFO"}]}'
```

Ava (CS): observed result: response for session B sometimes includes fragments from session A (e.g., "Order pizza" text appended). Customer provided req ids: req_abc123, req_def456. Happened in eu-west-1 hosted, model=redwood-neo-13b, route=/v1/chat/stream.

Liam (Eng): ack — assigning to eng-runtime for triage. Can you confirm this is with the same tenant/auth token?

Ava (CS): yes same tenant token, different x-session-id header. Repro rate ~30% at concurrency=2, ~90% at concurrency=20 for their load tests.

Noah (Product): this looks like a data leakage/compliance P1. Customer is a high-touch prospect, want ETA and mitigation path.

Maya (Sales): Everset is on a trial with high ARR potential. This blocks next-stage deployment. Please escalate.

Sam (DevOps): preliminary suspicion: cache key collision in the KV cache / session prefix normalization. What does x-session-id look like? Any truncation on our side?

Ava (CS): example headers they sent: "x-session-id: evs-user-42" and "x-session-id: evs-user-42-b". They also tried long uuids and saw lower repro, but not zero.

Liam (Eng): thanks. I'll reproduce in staging with a quick harness. Hypothesis: session id hashing truncates to 64 bits and we aren't salting per-tenant, leading to occasional collisions under load. Immediate mitigation options: 1) include full session id when forming cache key, 2) add per-tenant salt, 3) force single-connection session affinity for this tenant.

Ava (CS): customer requests workaround + ETA. They prefer not to disable concurrency.

Noah (Product): Launch criteria for a ship/fix: reproduction in staging, unit/regression tests added, canary deploy to 5% tenants, and no leak observed for 2 hours under simulated load. Workaround acceptable if we can apply in <4 hours.

Liam (Eng): I'll attempt hotfix to use the full session id in the cache key (fast path change). If that looks risky, fallback to per-tenant salt mapping. Estimate: 4-8 hours for PR + tests, then canary 1-2 hours.

deploy-bot: Created issue ENG-4123 in eng-runtime: "session-cache key collision causing prompt crossover". Labels: [bug, customer-impact, urgent]. Owner: Liam (Eng).

Sam (DevOps): I can enable a temporary routing flag to isolate Everset: routing-policy: session-isolation=true. That requires rolling restart of the worker pool in eu-west-1 (30m change window). Approve?

Noah (Product): approve the temporary isolation restart. Notify CS before restart.

Ava (CS): I'll message Everset and offer two options: 1) short-term: enable session-isolation flag (we'll coordinate restart), 2) long-term: apply fix in eng-runtime. Customer asked for ETA and will wait for mitigation.

Maya (Sales): I'll add notes to the account and pause the upcoming demo until we confirm mitigation.

Liam (Eng): Plan: (a) add regression that stresses cache keys with colliding suffixes, (b) implement full-key fix in eng-runtime, (c) run staging canary under 20x concurrency. I'll link PR to ENG-4123.

Sam (DevOps): applied session-isolation=true for evs-tenant at 2026-03-18T20:05Z — rolling restart started; no restarts beyond workers.

Ava (CS): quick update from Everset after the isolation flag: they re-ran their tests for 30 minutes under the same load, observed zero cross-session leakage during that window. They're satisfied with the short-term mitigation but want a permanent fix before GA.

Noah (Product): set priority to P1 and allocate resources for a permanent fix this sprint.

Liam (Eng): will push a PR today and request expedited review. I'll post links to PR and test results in this thread.

Ava (CS): thanks all — I'll keep the customer informed and move to close the loop when PR lands and canary completes.
